Let me analyze the conflict.

Axis: applicant
- Register: "Avery Berkel"
- Document: "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd"

The certificate document itself, in the visible context, shows the cert ID comments saying applicant: Avery Berkel, but the actual printed document context says the conflict is document: "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd". Wait — the context provided in the prompt has `<!-- applicant: Avery Berkel -->` as a comment, but the conflict states document: "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd". Hmm. Perhaps elsewhere on the certificate the applicant is stated as "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd". The extracted comments are metadata; the actual body may list the applicant differently.

Now: Avery Berkel is a brand/company. Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd is the legal entity — Avery Berkel is a brand of Avery Weigh-Tronix (formerly Weigh-Tronix, acquired Avery). Historically, Avery Berkel was a company name (Avery Berkel Ltd), later part of Weigh-Tronix, and now Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd. In 2009, the applicant likely was "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd" with brand "Avery Berkel" instruments. Are they the same entity? "Avery Berkel" vs "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd" — these are related but the names genuinely differ: Avery Berkel is a brand name/trading name; Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd is the legal company. The rules say: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

Is this "legal-suffix drift" or "spelling drift"? No — "Avery Berkel" vs "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd" is not suffix drift; the core names differ (Berkel vs Weigh-Tronix). They denote related entities: Avery Berkel is a brand of Avery Weigh-Tronix. In the OIML-CS database, the applicant might be registered as "Avery Berkel" while the certificate legally names "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd". For a fused record, which value should carry? The rule says document (certificate) is the legal instrument, so best_value = document's: "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd".

Verdict: different-entity — genuinely different company names (brand vs legal entity), so best_value from the document.

One could argue same-entity since Avery Berkel instruments are made by Avery Weigh-Tronix; but per the rules, "genuinely different company or person names" = different-entity. "Avery Berkel" vs "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd" — the names genuinely differ beyond spelling/suffix drift. Historically "Avery Berkel" was itself a company name (Avery Berkel Ltd) until renamed; by 2009 the legal entity was Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd. So they are not the same name; different-entity, best_value = document's.
